I am an old man, sixty-one years now, and I have been farming this small piece of land my whole life. My plot is small, less than half a hectare, and I grow my crop together with another one to make sure my family has something to eat even if one fails. I do not have money to buy fertilizer from the shop — none of us in my village use it on a plot like this — and I keep some manure from my few animals to put on the soil. I will use my own seed that I saved from last harvest, like my father did, and I will work the land with my own hands and the help of my wife.
